San Jorge is in the department of Rivas, on the shore of Lake Nicaragua, also known as Cocibolca. For travelers, it is chiefly the starting point for the crossing to Ometepe: ferries, passengers, and the everyday life of a small lakeside port come together at the docks.

Before departure, you can take in the lake's wide expanse from the waterfront and look toward the island. Fishing, water transport, and trade connect the town to the lake, while the road through Rivas links it to the Pacific coast. San Jorge fits naturally into an itinerary between Granada, Ometepe, and San Juan del Sur. The ferry timetable and arrival port on the island are confirmed when arranging the crossing.

## The Golden Altar in Casco Antiguo

San José Church stands in Panama City's historic quarter. Its principal attraction is the richly decorated gilded altar inside. The intricate carvings and warm golden color stand out against the light-colored walls.

A visit is easy to combine with a walk through Casco Viejo, where churches, squares, and historic streets are within walking distance of one another. We include San José in a six-hour city excursion alongside Panamá Viejo and the modern districts.

Admission to the church is included in this group excursion. We agree on the visiting time and the order of stops when preparing your trip.

San Juan Chamula is in Mexico's Chiapas State, among highland communities near San Cristóbal. The Church of St. John holds particular significance. Its religious life is closely tied to local rituals in which Catholic elements coexist with older beliefs.

A visit offers an introduction to the community's culture through its religious traditions and the surrounding village. Chamula often appears on itineraries alongside Zinacantán, where the focus is on weaving and embroidery. Together, these places show how local customs continue to thrive alongside the colonial towns of Chiapas.
